title: 1  Symbols, abbr. and formula
text:
Symbols and abbr

\(L\ or \ N =\) Labor units, in persons or hours
\(K=\) Amount of physical capital
\(H=\) Amount of human capital
\(N=\) Amount of Natural resources
\(MB=\) Marginal Benefit
\(MC=\) Marginal Cost
\(MP=\) Marginal Product
\(HH_s\ or\ hh_s=\) house holds
\(PPF=\) Production possibility Frontier
\(D=\) Demand curve
\(GDP=\) Gross Domestic Product
\(GNP=\) Gross National Product
\(GNR=\) Net govt revenue or income
\(Y=\) Consumers’ income, National Income, or GDP
\(C=\) consumption
\(\mathrm{I}=\) investment
\(G=\) Government purchases
\(NX=\) Net exports, which is (X-M)
\(X=\) value of exports
\(M=\) value of imports
\(CPI=\) Consumer Price Index
\(Y/N=\) Output per person, (Labor) Productivity
\(K/N=\) Capital per worker (per person)
\(H/N=\) Human capital per person
\(i=\) Nominal interest rate
\(r=\) Real interest rate
\(\pi=\) Inflation or sometimes profit
\(P=\) Price of a good or the price level
\(G=\) government purchases

\(G\&S=\) Goods and services
\(Govt=\) government
\(Q=\) Quantity or amount of the good or service
\(S_{pvt}=\) Private saving
\(S_{gov} \ or \ S_{pub}=\) Public or government saving
\(T=\) Net taxes, which is (Taxes-govt transfers)
\(RGDP=\) Real GDP
\(NGDP=\) Nominal GDP
\(S=\) Supply Curve, or National Saving (in another context)
\(W=\) Nominal Wage
\(w=\) Real wage
\(A=\) Technology or Total factor productivity
\(TFP=\) Total factor productivity



Formula*
\[
\begin{align*}
Y &= C + I + G + NX \\
   where\ NX= X- M
\end{align*}
\]

\(GDP = sum\ of\ P\times Q\), for all goods
\(GDP\ deflator= \frac{NGDP}{RGDP}\times 100\)
if \(Z= X\cdot Y  \Rightarrow  \%\Delta Z \approx \%\Delta X + \%\Delta Y\)
if \(Z= X/Y \Rightarrow \%\Delta Z \approx \%\Delta X - \%\Delta Y\)

\[
\begin{align*}
GNP &= GDP + \text{Net factor payments from abroad} \\
    &= GDP + \text{Income of domestic factors earned abroad} \\
    &\qquad - \text{Income of foreign factors earned at home}
\end{align*}
\]

\(Y_d = Y + NFP + TR + INT - T\)

\(GNR = T-TR-INT\)

\(GNR + Y_d = GDP + NFP = GNP\)

\(S_{pvt} = (Y + NFP − T + TR + INT ) − C\)

\(S_{govt} = (T − TR − INT ) − G\)

Sources of S, national saving: \[
\begin{align*}
S &= Spvt + Sgovt \\
  &= (Y + NFP − T + TR + INT − C) + (T − TR − INT − G)  \\
  &= GNP − C − G
\end{align*}
\]
Uses of S:
\[
\begin{align*}
S &= GNP − C − G \\  
  &= (Y + NFP) − C − G  \\
  &= (C + I + G + NX + NFP) − C − G  \\
  &= (I + NX + NFP)  \\
  &= (I + CA)
\end{align*}
\]
\(Prod.\ function: \ Y = AF(K,N)\)
C-D prod. function: \(Y = AK^α N^{1−α}\) + \(u-rate= 100\times \frac{\# Unemployed}{\# Labor\ Force}\) + \(L.F\ partic.\ rate= 100\times \frac{\# Labor\ Force}{\# Adult\ popn}\)
\[
\begin{align*}
Cyclical & \ unemployment = u-u^{*}  \\
      & where, u = \text{actual unempl}  \\
    & and\ u^*= \text{Natural of unemployment}\\
and & \\
\frac{Y − Y^{*}}{Y^{*}} & = −2(u − u^{∗}) \\
and \ \frac{\Delta Y}{Y}&= 3 − 2 · Δu
\end{align*}
\]
Chapter 4:
For closed Economy: \[
\begin{align}
S &= S_{hh} + S_{gov} \\
  &= (Y − T − C) + (T − G) \\
  &= Y − C − G
\end{align}
\]

\(Uc ≡ r · P_k + d · P_k = (r + d) · PK\)

With tax on capital:

\(MPK^f = \frac{r+d}{1-\tau} P_k\)
\(K_{t+1} = K_t + I_t - dK_t \Rightarrow  I_t = K_{t+1}-(1+d)K_t\)
\(Tobin’s\ q = \frac{V}{P_k \cdot K}\)

Equilibrium:

\(AD=AS \Rightarrow \bar{Y} = C(r) + I(r) + G \Rightarrow S=I\)

Chapter 7: Asset Markets:

\(\Delta Y/Y = \Delta A/A + \epsilon_{K} \cdot \Delta K/K + \epsilon_{N}  \cdot \Delta N/N \qquad (2)\)
Steady state: \(sf (k) = (n + d)k\)
Golen rule: \(MPK = (n + d)\)
\(\frac{M_d}{P} = L_d(Y, r + \pi^e)\)
\(\Delta M/M - \Delta P/P = \epsilon_Y \Delta Y/Y + \epsilon_i \Delta i/i\)
\(V= \frac{P \times Y }{ M}\)

Chapter 9: IS-LM model:

\(IS curve: S(r; etc) = I(r; etc)\)
\(M_S/P=M_d/P \Rightarrow L(r-; Y+,\pi^e -)\)
